source.note: Chosen over example_sentences + entry_sentences: that pairing is 95% Tatoeba, largely traditional script, numbered pinyin only, and its links are substring matches rather than sense alignment. See the header of src/build/sentences.ts for the full comparison.
source.license: SayMei production data; sentences are SayMei-owned, not CC-CEDICT.

grading.definition: ZSG = the highest HSK 3.0 (2026) band of any content token after segmentation, clamped to 1-7. Computed from the canon word list plus the sentence text; no model, no copied grade.
grading.segmenter: Forward maximum matching over the canon's own simplified forms. Unmatched single characters take the lowest band of any canon word containing them.
grading.beyondHsk: A character no canon word contains is outside HSK 3.0; it forces the grade to 7 and is counted in beyondHskTokens.
grading.newWordCount: Per band prefix 1..7, the count of DISTINCT content token forms outside that prefix. A value of 1 is an i+1 sentence. Tokens outside HSK 3.0 count against every prefix, including 7.
grading.selection: Candidates are filtered by the quality gate (see `quality` below), then up to 3 per headword are spread over the difficulty key (zsg, newWordCount["1"]): lowest, highest, middle. Both parts ship in every record. A headword with one distinct key ships one sentence; a single-character headword ships one sentence by rule; a headword whose every candidate is flagged ships its least-flagged one.
grading.charLengthPercentile: Mid-rank percentile of the sentence's character count against every GRADED sentence of the same ZSG band — the full pool, not the shipped subset, which is chosen partly on length. Measured on this corpus rather than imported from the dialogue corpus.

quality.note: Applied during selection, not afterwards: every rule below decides which of a headword's candidate sentences ship, and data/sentences.jsonl is already the filtered corpus. The rules and their evidence live in src/build/quality.ts; the judged measurement they were derived from is data/quality-report.json.

rules.rule: The headword is immediately followed by a personal title, or preceded by 姓 or 叫 — it has been pressed into service as a surname.
rules.evidence: 18 of 18 flagged sample links are broken (100%), against a 12.85% corpus base rate.

rules.rule: The sentence grades below the headword's own band, so the headword is the hardest thing in it and everything around it is filler.
rules.evidence: 13 of 16 flagged sample links are broken (81%).

rules.rule: The headword does not survive canon segmentation as its own token: it is buried inside a longer HSK word, and the sentence teaches that word instead.
rules.evidence: 30 of 48 flagged sample links are broken (63%).

rules.rule: Same test against CC-CEDICT's 120,400 headwords rather than the 11,092 HSK ones: 训 inside 校训, 焊 inside 焊接, 知识 inside 知识分子 — compounds the canon is too small to see.
rules.evidence: 39 of 81 flagged sample links are broken (48%); it flags 33 links the canon test misses, 9 of them broken (27%).

rules.rule: The sentence's own pinyin reads the headword as a different word — 担 as dàn not dān, 地 as dì not de, 正 as zhēng not zhèng.
rules.evidence: 11 of 21 flagged sample links are broken (52%); 10 of 16 among single-character headwords (63%).

rules.rule: The sentence is in the bottom decile of length for its own grade band — a frame with the headword dropped into it rather than a sentence about anything. 这是自助。 是 five characters.
rules.evidence: 8 of 27 flagged sample links are broken (30%) among multi-character headwords, against 5.6% for the rest.

rules.rule: Blank the headword out and the same sentence is filed under another headword too: it is a template the source stamped across the word list, not a sentence written for this word.
rules.evidence: Among single-character headwords that clear every hard rule, 10 of 16 links on a shared frame are broken (63%) against 11 of 67 on a unique one (16%).

selection.note: Pools are tried in order — clean, then hard-clean, then everything — and the last pool ships exactly one sentence, so no rule can take a headword's last link. A selected link carrying a flag is a headword whose whole pool carried it.

sourceHskLevelAgreement.note: The source rows carry their own hskLevel. It is never trusted, only compared: this is a check on the computed grade, not an input to it.

measuredQuality.note: A judged defect rate for exactly this corpus. Same prompt, model, temperature, stratification and estimator as data/quality-report.json; a new seed, because the filter this corpus was built with was chosen partly by looking at the old sample. Re-run with `npx tsx src/build/quality.ts --remeasure`.

sampling.unit: headword link (one sentence paired with one canon headword it was selected for)
sampling.design: Stratified random sample. Strata are HSK band group of the headword (1-3 / 4-6 / 7) crossed with headword character length (1 / 2 / 3+). Allocation is a floor per stratum plus the remainder proportional to stratum population; corpus-wide rates are population-weighted with a finite-population correction.

results.definition: broken = the judge says the sentence is ungrammatical, incoherent, or misuses the headword. awkward = parseable but stilted. good = natural Mandarin. notClean = broken + awkward.

measuredQuality.comparison: The same instrument on the corpus that shipped before the quality gate measured 12.85% broken (95% CI 10.08%-15.63%, n=600, seed "zhongdex-quality-v1"), with 12.11% further awkward. This measurement is a fresh draw on a new seed against the filtered corpus, so it is like-for-like on everything but the corpus and the seed.
